newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian minister says she was tortured in 1974.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian minister says she was tortured in 1974.

text.p: An Ethiopian government minister told the trial of the country's former "Dergue" military rulers on Tuesday that she was whipped and both her arms were broken in torture sessions in 1974.

"I was blindfolded and a smelly piece of cloth was thrust in my mouth. My hands were tied behind my back and I was hung suspended in a middle of a room," said the witness, who under court rules cannot be identified by name.
"They took turns and beat me with truncheons until the skin on my back was flayed and blood dripping from my body soiled the floor," said the witness.
She was testifying at the trial in Addis Ababa of 71 former Dergue military junta officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity. They face the death penalty if they are found guilty.
Only 46 of the 71 accused are in court. The others including dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam, who ruled Ethiopia from 1977 to 1991 and now lives in Zaimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
The witness said she taught at Addis Ababa university in 1974 when police found a tract advocating the equality of women when they ransacked her home.
She said she was taken to Dergue headquarters and tortured to force her to say she was a member of an opposition Marxist group and an agent for the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency.
Both her arms were broken and the soles of her feet were shredded, she said. She was released in 1981 after being forced to sign a statement.
The trial was adjourned until Thursday.
Ethiopian prosecutors have charged 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide under the Dergue.
